summary: Python library that runs very large language models on small GPUs by loading the model one layer at a time.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: AirLLM cuts the GPU memory needed for LLM inference by splitting a model into layers and streaming them through the GPU. The README says this lets 70B models run on a single 4GB GPU without quantization, distillation or pruning, and it now also supports training on small VRAM.
sixtySeconds.problem: Big open models normally need expensive GPUs with lots of memory. AirLLM trades speed and disk space for memory so you can try them on modest hardware.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when GPU memory, not time, is your limit. It loads models with one AutoModel line from Hugging Face IDs or local paths.
requirements: An NVIDIA GPU, or Apple silicon on macOS
Plenty of disk space for the layer-split model

overview: Install with pip, then load a model with AutoModel.from_pretrained using a Hugging Face repo ID or a local path, and call generate as with a regular transformers model.

On first use the original model is decomposed and saved layer by layer, so make sure the Hugging Face cache has enough disk space. Optional block-wise compression can speed inference by up to 3x per the README.
On macOS, install mlx and torch; only Apple silicon and Llama-style models are supported there. The project is Apache 2.0 licensed.

tutorial.title: Generate text with a large model
tutorial.useCase: Load a model by Hugging Face ID and generate an answer.
setup: Free disk space in the Hugging Face cache

steps.title: Write the script
steps.code:
from airllm import AutoModel

MAX_LENGTH = 128
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-32B")

input_tokens = model.tokenizer(['What is the capital of United States?'],
    return_tensors="pt", return_attention_mask=False,
    truncation=True, max_length=MAX_LENGTH, padding=False)

generation_output = model.generate(
    input_tokens['input_ids'].to(model.device),
    max_new_tokens=20, use_cache=True, return_dict_in_generate=True)

print(model.tokenizer.decode(generation_output.sequences[0]))

steps.title: Run it
steps.body: The first run downloads the model and splits it into layers, which takes time and disk space.

tutorial.expected: The script prints the model's answer.

troubleshooting.problem: Out of disk space on first run
troubleshooting.solution: The model is split and saved layer-wise; free space in the Hugging Face cache or set layer_shards_saving_path.

troubleshooting.problem: Error on macOS with a non-Llama model
troubleshooting.solution: Only Llama-style models run on macOS for now.
